shows: Far zoom carries traffic as city state: road-level congestion only, no vehicle glyphs, no signals, no stop bars.

view: The Loop and River North, z14.6
shows: Mid zoom reads as flow: a sampled subset of vehicles, congestion on roads, no signal system yet.
Close zoom: full class glyphs at lane centres, queues stacking from the stop line, approach signal heads.
Signal heads belong to their own approach: a small dark housing with one bright lamp at the kerbside, plus a transverse stop line — never a coloured blob in the junction.
Class silhouettes at close zoom: car with tapered nose and windshield, truck as cab plus box, bicycle as a thin frame with wire wheels.

view: Approach queue at a signal, z17.2
shows: Queue packing from the authoritative rank: front vehicle at the stop line, each next one stacked behind by its own class length with a small gap, no overlap.
Vehicles curving through the junction on a quadratic path, leaving aligned with the new road instead of cutting the corner.
The same transition on the opposite turn sense, with heading taken from the curve tangent.
Expressway flow stays legible: no signals on mainline, ramps narrower than the main carriageways, traffic inside its own direction.
Congestion as the primary far-zoom signal: only roads under pressure tint warm, amber, orange or red; free-flowing roads stay neutral.
A crash is a small anchored hazard glyph with a slight road tint — map-native notation, no ring, no pulse.
A closure crosses the physical road with a short red band and a barrier marker; it does not cover half the intersection.

view: Bridge closed on the river, z15.6
shows: The whole logical crossing reads as closed, with one small label naming it and traffic rerouting off the approach.

view: Event lets out at a real venue, z15.2
shows: An event is a small static venue badge on real geography, with traffic emerging on the surrounding streets — no pulse ring, no purple effect.
